FR-001.title: Status lists a recorded decision captured in the structured form the pipeline writes, showing its decision text

FR-002.title: Status keeps listing plain-text decisions exactly as it does today

FR-003.title: Status lists every decision from a context mixing both stored forms, preserving recorded order

FR-004.title: Status leaves out a decision entry with no usable text and still lists the rest

FR-005.title: Status does not change its Decisions output shape beyond making hidden decisions appear

FR-006.title: A decision's why and rejected detail stays reachable for a future verbose report

FR-007.title: Every reader of the run's other recorded lists is audited for the same string-only assumption

FR-008.title: Status never fails the command that runs it, on any shape of recorded data

intent: Make the status report show the decisions a run actually recorded, in every stored form, instead of reporting none.
expectations: The Decisions section stays one line per decision — a verbose why/rejected report is separate work
No change to how decisions are recorded, only to how they are read back
No de-duplication, reordering, or truncation of recorded decisions
context: area: speckit-extension/scripts — the capture read side (status-context.py) and its writers (capture.py, write-context.py)
constraint: the read side never raises and never exits non-zero
approach: Widen the status reader's decisions filter to accept both stored forms — a bare string renders as itself, an entry object renders its decision text, anything with no usable text is skipped — mirroring the rule the VS Code viewer's reader already uses. The report block and the machine-readable RESOLUTION line keep their exact shape, so resume and the test suite see no contract change. Sibling readers of the other captured lists are audited in the same pass and fixed only where they actually share the assumption.

decisions.decision: Mirror the viewer reader's accept-both-shapes rule instead of inventing a second one
decisions.why: the viewer and the status report read the same field, and two independent derivations of one fact drift; the viewer's version has been correct all along
decisions.rejected: writing a bespoke widening in the Python reader, or normalizing decisions to plain strings at write time (which would discard why/rejected)

decisions.decision: Keep _decisions returning display strings so the RESOLUTION line's element type is unchanged
decisions.why: resume parses that line and both the tests and the TypeScript side treat decisions as a list of strings; silently changing it would be a contract break inside a fix for a silent contract break
decisions.rejected: returning entry dicts and flattening at the print boundary

decisions.decision: Skip an unusable entry rather than letting it blank or break the section
decisions.why: the defect being fixed is a whole section disappearing; a fix that trades one silent blanking for another is not worth shipping
decisions.rejected: failing loudly on a malformed entry, or dropping the whole list when any entry is bad

decisions.decision: Treat the sibling-reader sweep as an audit that reports, not speculative widening
decisions.why: doctor_drift.py already branches on dict for verified[], and expectations/context go through a string-only writer so their shape is guaranteed — widening them would add branches no honest test can reach
decisions.rejected: widening every list reader for symmetry

decisions.decision: Prove the new mixed-form test fails against the pre-fix reader before landing the fix
decisions.why: the defect survived because the fixture population was all strings and could not see it; a test that only ever ran against fixed code would repeat that mistake

decisions.decision: Drop a bare number or boolean decision instead of stringifying it, as the old filter did
decisions.why: the viewer reader this one now mirrors accepts only strings and entry objects, so keeping the numeric passthrough would make the two surfaces disagree about which decisions exist — and a boolean rendering as the line "True" was never a decision anyone wrote
decisions.rejected: preserving the int/float passthrough for strict output parity with the old filter

plan.summary: One reader widened to accept both stored decision forms, mirroring the viewer rule, with the report and RESOLUTION contracts held byte-stable
plan.key_finding: capture.py always stores decisions as objects, so the string-only filter dropped every real run — only hand-authored fixtures ever rendered, which is why every test was green
